record.paper_title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Every polycyclic group can be embedded into GL(n, Z) for some natural number n, and matrix representations can be computed in some special cases such as torsion-free nilpotent groups. Determine the computational complexity of finding a matrix representation of a polycyclic group.

evidence.quote: It is well-known that every polycyclic group can be embed- ded into GL(n, Z) for some n ∈ N.
For groups that are additionally torsion-free and nilpotent, a matrix representation can be computed.
(6) What is the complexity of finding matrix representation of polycyclic groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A group $G$ is called polycyclic if it admits a subnormal series
$$G = G_0 \triangleright G_1 \triangleright \cdots \triangleright G_k = \{1\}$$
in which every quotient $G_{i}/G_{i+1}$ is cyclic. Every polycyclic group can be presented by a finite polycyclic presentation, and it is a classical theorem of Auslander and Swan that every polycyclic group is isomorphic to a subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{Z})$ for some positive integer $n$. By a faithful integer matrix representation of a polycyclic group $G$ we mean an injective homomorphism $\rho: G \hookrightarrow GL(n,\mathbb{Z})$ for some $n$, where the images of a fixed finite generating set of $G$ are specified as explicit integer matrices.

Problem. Given as input a finite polycyclic presentation of a polycyclic group $G$, determine the computational complexity (with respect to the bit length of the input) of producing a faithful representation $\rho: G \to GL(n,\mathbb{Z})$, i.e., output an integer $n$ and explicit integer matrices for the images of the generators of $G$ that define an injective homomorphism. Provide upper and lower bounds on the time complexity, the bit-size of $n$, and the bit-size of the matrix entries (as functions of the size of the input presentation), or show that no such bounds (e.g., polynomial) can hold in general.
artifact.status_search_result: Practical algorithms for computing integer matrix representations of polycyclic groups are known (e.g., the GAP "polycyclic" package implements such methods, building on work by Lo–Ostheimer and Eick), and constructions are well understood for torsion-free nilpotent groups. However, no rigorous complexity bounds (polynomial, exponential, or otherwise) on producing a faithful matrix representation from a polycyclic presentation in general appear to be established in the literature. The question of the computational complexity is listed as an open problem in surveys on polycyclic group-based cryptography.

status_evidence.title: A Practical Algorithm for Finding Matrix Representations for Polycyclic Groups
status_evidence.snippet: A practical algorithm exists for constructing a representation by integer matrices for a polycyclic group given by a finite presentation.
status_evidence.claim: Practical (but not complexity-analyzed) algorithms for the construction exist.

status_evidence.title: GAP polycyclic package – Matrix Representations
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms in GAP to compute matrix representations of polycyclic groups.
status_evidence.claim: Implementations exist but their worst-case complexity is not characterized.
